name: Oath-Binding (Recht)
laws: A formally sworn oath has metaphysical weight
Breaking an oath incurs theological cost as well as legal
The witnesses matter — oaths sworn before gods are heavier
Some oaths cannot be unmade; others can be formally released
costs: Broken oaths leave visible marks to those with sight
limits: Cannot force compliance; the oath-taker can still break, at cost
Cannot oath-bind those who have not consented
examples: Havald's veteran oath to the Emperor

name: Götterkriege Cosmology
laws: Gods exist as active agents with factions
Divine conflict propagates at every scale
The mortal political is the shadow of the divine political
costs: Mortal champions pay the price of divine conflict
Neutrality is not possible for the chosen
Victory for one divine faction is defeat for another, cascading consequences
limits: Gods cannot directly intervene; they must work through agents
Divine power is finite and contested
Certain mortal oaths bind even gods
examples: Askir empire as stage for divine faction conflict
